concepts.title: Distance vs Displacement
concepts.body: Distance is the total path traveled by an object, regardless of direction, and is always a positive scalar quantity. Displacement, on the other hand, is the shortest distance between the initial and final positions of an object and includes direction, making it a vector quantity. For example, if you walk around a circular park and return to your starting point, your distance is the circumference of the park, but your displacement is zero.

concepts.title: Speed vs Velocity
concepts.body: Speed is a scalar quantity that measures how fast an object is moving, calculated as distance divided by time. Velocity is a vector quantity that measures the rate of change of displacement, including direction. For instance, a car traveling at 60 km/h north has both speed and velocity, but if it changes direction, its velocity changes even if its speed remains the same.

concepts.title: Acceleration
concepts.body: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity with respect to time. Uniform acceleration occurs when the velocity changes by equal amounts in equal intervals of time, while non-uniform acceleration involves unequal changes. For example, a car speeding up at a constant rate experiences uniform acceleration, but if it speeds up unevenly, it has non-uniform acceleration.

formulas.title: Speed and Average Velocity
formulas.body: Speed = Distance / Time (speed in m/s, distance in m, time in s). Average Velocity = Displacement / Time (velocity in m/s, displacement in m, time in s). These formulas are used to calculate how fast an object is moving and its direction of motion.

formulas.title: Equations of Motion
formulas.body: v = u + a t (v in m/s, u in m/s, a in m/s^2, t in s). s = u t + (1/2) a t^2 (s in m, u in m/s, a in m/s^2, t in s). These equations describe the motion of an object under uniform acceleration, helping to predict its velocity and position at any given time.

examples.title: Everyday Example
examples.body: When you ride a bicycle, you apply force to the pedals, causing the wheels to rotate and move forward. The cause of motion here is the force applied by your legs.

examples.title: Applied Example
examples.body: A rocket launching into space accelerates due to the thrust generated by its engines. The cause of this acceleration is the expulsion of gases at high speed from the rocket's engines.

mcqs.question: What is the SI unit of speed?
mcqs.explanation: The SI unit of speed is meters per second (m/s). km/h is a common unit but not SI, m/s^2 is for acceleration, and km/s is not a standard unit for speed.

mcqs.question: A car travels 60 km north and then 20 km south. What is its displacement?
mcqs.explanation: Displacement is the shortest distance between the initial and final positions. The car travels 60 km north and 20 km south, so its displacement is 40 km north. The other options either ignore direction or add distances incorrectly.

mcqs.question: An object accelerates uniformly from rest to 10 m/s in 5 seconds. What is its acceleration?
mcqs.explanation: Using the formula a = (v - u) / t, where v = 10 m/s, u = 0 m/s, and t = 5 s, the acceleration is 2 m/s^2. The other options result from incorrect calculations or misunderstanding the formula.
